summary: Scanner consumes the revocation feed and fails closed past a staleness ceiling
description:
Split from **TKT-162** on the owner's instruction (2026-08-22). TKT-162 builds the **feed**; this ticket **consumes** it and is where the gate behaviour actually changes.

**Blocked by TKT-162** — there is nothing to pull until the feed exists.

**Owner decisions (binding, taken 2026-08-22):**
1. **Fail closed** past the staleness ceiling — a scanner whose revocation view is too old refuses rather than admitting on a stale list.
2. **Generous ceiling** — refunds cluster days ahead of the performance, so a start-of-shift pull closes most of the gap. The ceiling is a backstop, not a hot path. **The number itself is still open** and is this ticket's first shaping question.
3. **Operator override past the ceiling, and the override is RECORDED** — a connectivity outage must not close the door with no local mitigation, and an override that lands in the trail is auditable.

**Why the ceiling lives here and not in the feed.** `scanner_devices.last_seen_at` is server-side, best-effort, and documented *"Advisory only… Never read by any decision"*. It records when the server last **heard from** a device — not when the device last **successfully pulled**. Only the scanner holds that fact, so only the scanner can bound the age of its own view.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] The scanner pulls the revocation feed on the same `online` edge that already drives queue sync (`web/scanner/src/App.tsx`), and on a manual action, storing the result durably beside the occurrence queue.
- [ ] An offline scan of a ticket **on the stored revocation list** is refused, without a network round-trip, and the operator is told *why* in words distinguishable from "not paired" and from "already redeemed".
- [ ] A scanner whose last successful pull is **older than the ceiling** refuses **every** scan — fail closed — and says so.
- [ ] Past the ceiling an **operator override** admits a single scan, and the override is **recorded** so it reaches the trail rather than evaporating on the device. A recorded override is a new fact: decide whether it is a lifecycle event value, an alarm, or a field on the occurrence, and say why. (Adding a *value* to `event_type` changes no signed bytes — the canonical form treats it as a free string — so the cheap option is available if it is the right one.)
- [ ] The refusal is **not** a silent drop: an occurrence refused on the revocation list must still be reconcilable/visible, consistent with TKT-269's "an offline admit is never silent" and ADR-025's recording posture. Say explicitly what is recorded for a *refused* scan versus an *overridden* one.
- [ ] **`make browser` + a spec in `test/browser/`** that drives the write paths through a real browser — per AGENTS.md, a web-UI ticket is not verified until a browser has submitted its forms, and a browser spec cannot see a request the SSR handler makes, so assert what the browser can see or what the write left behind.

**Open shaping questions (not yet answered):**
- **The ceiling number.** Owner said "generous"; the value is undecided. Candidate framing: long enough that a normal connectivity blip never reaches it, short enough to bound a refunded holder's window. Refund timing (days ahead) suggests hours rather than minutes.
- **Does the feed carry exchanged ids too?** TKT-270 closes the alarm half for exchanges. If the answer is yes, TKT-162's contract may need to change — check before that ticket merges, not after.
- **What does the scanner do on its very first pull ever** (no prior state, ceiling trivially exceeded)? A brand-new device must not be born refusing.

Quality gates: `make check` green; **`make browser` green**; contract tests.

objective.note: This is where the hole actually closes. TKT-269 made an offline admit of a refunded ticket visible; TKT-162 makes the state available; only this ticket stops the admission.

scope.note: Scanner-side only, but the boundary has one genuinely undecided edge: whether a refused-on-revocation scan is recorded differently from an ordinary refusal, and what an overridden admission records. That is a trail-semantics decision, not a UI one.

uncertainties.note: THREE open, one of which is the owner's. (a) THE CEILING NUMBER — 'generous' was decided, the value was not; hours rather than minutes is implied by refunds clustering days ahead, but the number is a product call about venue connectivity. (b) Does the feed carry EXCHANGED ids as well as refunded — this must be settled BEFORE TKT-162 merges, or its contract changes afterwards. (c) First-pull-ever behaviour: a brand-new device has no prior pull and trivially exceeds any ceiling; it must not be born refusing, and the rule that prevents that is a design decision.

dependencies.note: Blocked by TKT-162 (the feed) — a real blocker, linked. Nothing else. TKT-269 is Done and independent; TKT-270 is independent but see uncertainty (b).

approach.note: Blocked on the uncertainties above, and deliberately NOT `deferred`: this decides who gets through a door, which is the auth surface where shaping.md forbids the escape hatch. Known direction: pull on the existing `online` handler in web/scanner/src/App.tsx (~:106-200), store beside the IndexedDB occurrence queue (src/occurrences.ts), consult before the offline admit decision. The QR credential carries `tid` (services/access/internal/ticket/token.go:14) so the check is a local set lookup with no decode beyond what the scanner already does.

first_slice.note: Plausibly splits again: (i) pull + store + refuse on list, (ii) ceiling + override. (i) closes the common case and needs no override semantics; (ii) is the outage path. Decide at shaping once the ceiling number exists.

success.note: ACs are drafted but two depend on open decisions — the ceiling AC needs a number to be testable, and the override AC needs the recording decision before its assertion can be written. The browser-spec AC is firm regardless.

context_memo.note: Inherit TKT-162's governingAdrs, then ADD the web/scanner browser-testing rules from AGENTS.md and ADR-025 §D3 (occurrence identity, actuation keyed on the device's own durable pending record). RE-VERIFY at claim time rather than trusting this snapshot.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Blocker cleared — but the ticket is still NOT ready (six items `open`)

Backlog review 2026-08-25 at HEAD `ad849f98`.

**Removed the stale `blocked-by: TKT-162`.** TKT-162 is **Done** and the feed it was blocked on exists: `GET /scans/voided-tickets` is mounted at `services/access/internal/api/server.go:127`, with organizer-spoof coverage at `server_smoke_test.go:297-298`. The link was left behind when that ticket merged, and a stale blocker is not harmless here — the board hard-blocks the Gate 1 drag on an open blocker, so this ticket was unpromotable for a reason that had stopped being true.

**That does not make it ready, and the distinction matters.** Six of eight `readiness` items are still `open`, three of them carrying owner decisions the shaping pass correctly refused to invent:

- **The ceiling number.** "Generous" was decided on 2026-08-22; the value was not. Hours or days changes what the AC can even assert.
- **Whether a refused-on-revocation scan is recorded**, and where.
- **The override's shape** — decided that it exists and is recorded, not what it looks like at the device.

`approach` is deliberately **not** `deferred`: this decides who gets through a door, which is an access-control surface, and `shaping.md` forbids the escape hatch on exactly those.

**So: unblocked, not ready.** The next move is the owner answering the three questions above (or a spike on the ceiling), not a Gate 1 drag.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=decision -->
### ✅ OWNER DECISION taken 2026-08-26 — the staleness ceiling is 24 HOURS

**Decision: a scanner whose revocation feed is more than 24 hours stale fails closed.**

**Rationale, as given:** generous enough that a venue with flaky connectivity finishes a normal event
day without locking itself out, tight enough that a scanner that has been offline since yesterday
stops trusting its list. This is the "hours rather than minutes" the 2026-08-22 decision implied,
made specific.

**This unblocks uncertainty (a) and the AC that depends on it.** The ceiling AC can now be written and
tested: at 24h − ε the scanner admits on its cached list; past 24h it refuses.

**Two of the three uncertainties remain open**, and they are smaller than the ceiling was:
- **(b) Is a refused-on-revocation scan recorded differently from an ordinary refusal, and where?**
- **(c) What does the override look like at the device?** It was decided that an override exists and
  is recorded — not what the scanner operator actually sees or does.

**Recommendation for the split the ticket already proposes, now that the number exists:** ship
**(i) pull + store + refuse on list** first. It closes the common case, needs neither (b) nor (c), and
is testable end to end. **(ii) ceiling + override** follows with the answers to (b) and (c).

The ceiling itself belongs to slice (ii), so slice (i) can be shaped and run immediately.

**Testing note that decides the fixture.** A 24-hour ceiling cannot be tested by waiting. The clock
must be injectable, or the staleness computed from a stored timestamp the test writes directly — and
per AGENTS.md, check which: TKT-233's precedent is that an expiry decided entirely in SQL has no
Go-side clock to inject. Establish that at shaping rather than at drafting.

**Blocker status:** TKT-162 is Done and the feed is mounted
(`services/access/internal/api/server.go:127`). Nothing else blocks this.
